excludedChapters.reason: This app accepts no uploads, generates no files, and builds no filesystem path from request data; static assets are served by the framework from the build output alone.
There is no OAuth or OIDC anywhere in this app: it issues its own session token after a local password check and is never an authorization server or a relying party.

boundaries.name: HTTP API
boundaries.untrusted: any HTTP client on the network: request bodies, path and query parameters, and the session cookie or bearer token presented with them
boundaries.trusted: everything below lib/db.ts, which performs no authorization checks of its own
assets: task rows belonging to other users

boundaries.name: Page request boundary
boundaries.untrusted: an unauthenticated browser requesting an authenticated route directly, before any page HTML is produced
boundaries.trusted: the server components rendered for /tasks, which assume a valid session
assets: the authenticated page shell and the task list rendered into it

controls.note: Values are interpolated through the framework’s escaping renderer; the app contains no raw HTML injection point.
The only dynamically built URL is the login redirect, whose parameter is set through the URL API rather than string concatenation.
Responses are produced by the framework’s JSON serializer; no JavaScript or JSON is assembled as text.
All database access goes through Prisma Client; no raw SQL string is built anywhere in the app.

controls.rationale: The application makes no operating-system calls: it has no shell-out, no subprocess and no command execution path at runtime.
There is no WYSIWYG editor and no field that accepts HTML; every text field is stored and rendered as plain text.

controls.note: No eval or dynamic code execution feature is used anywhere in the application source.

controls.rationale: The application parses no XML at all: every request and response body is JSON.

controls.note: The threat-boundary section states which inputs are untrusted and how each is validated before use.
Malformed bodies and unknown enum values are rejected with 400 rather than coerced, and the integration suite asserts it.
Validation runs in the API layer; the client is never trusted to have validated anything.

controls.rationale: The application has no multi-step business flow: every operation is a single authenticated request that is complete on its own.

controls.note: No Content-Security-Policy, Content-Disposition or Sec-Fetch validation is applied to any response.
Text is rendered through the framework’s text nodes; the app never assigns to innerHTML.
The session cookie is named "session" and carries neither the __Host- nor the __Secure- prefix.
No Strict-Transport-Security header is emitted by the application.

controls.rationale: The application sets no CORS headers and serves its client from its own origin, so there is no Access-Control-Allow-Origin value to get wrong.

This application does rely on the CORS preflight mechanism — a JSON content type on every mutating request — so this requirement’s precondition does not hold; the preflight case is answered at V3.5.2.

controls.note: The defence is that mutating endpoints require application/json, which is not a CORS-safelisted content type. Nothing tests that a text/plain body is actually rejected, so the mitigation is asserted rather than proven.
Every state-changing operation uses POST, PATCH or DELETE; no GET endpoint mutates anything.
Every response with a body is produced by the framework’s JSON responder, which sets application/json.

controls.rationale: The application opens no WebSocket connections; all traffic is request/response HTTP.

controls.note: No documentation defines rate limiting, anti-automation or adaptive response for the login endpoint.

controls.rationale: There is no user-facing path that sets a password: accounts are seeded, so no minimum length can be enforced at a place the user reaches.

controls.note: The application has no change-password function at all.

controls.rationale: There is no password change function for this rule to govern; its absence is recorded at V6.2.2.
There is no registration or password change path at which a candidate password could be checked against a breached-password list.
No composition rules exist because no user-facing path sets a password.

controls.note: The password field uses a masked password input.
The login form installs no paste, autocomplete or password-manager blocking handler.
The submitted password is verified exactly as received; only the email is normalised.
No credential-stuffing or brute-force control is implemented in the application.
Seeded accounts with known passwords ship with the repository (prisma/seed.mjs) so the E2E suites have something to log in as.

controls.rationale: The application generates no initial passwords or activation codes; credentials only ever arrive through the seed.

controls.note: There are no password hints and no knowledge-based authentication anywhere in the app.
Every token is verified on the server; the client never decides whether a session is valid.
A fresh token is generated per login and carries per-session claims; no static API key or shared secret stands in for a session.

controls.rationale: Reference tokens are not used: the session is a self-contained signed token, which is answered under V9.

controls.note: A new token is issued on authentication, but the previous self-contained token is not terminated and stays valid until its own expiry.
Logout deletes the cookie. A token captured beforehand remains accepted until it expires, because nothing maintains a terminated-token list or a per-user signing key.

controls.rationale: The application has no way to disable or delete a user account, so there is no event that should terminate that user’s sessions.

controls.note: The member and admin rules, and the ownership rule for task rows, are written down and implemented in one place.
Every task route checks the caller’s permission before acting.
Cross-user access to a task by id is rejected, and the integration suite proves it for read and for both mutations.
Authorization is enforced in the API layer; no client-side check is load-bearing.
The signature is verified before the payload is read (a node:crypto HMAC-SHA256 over a base64url payload, with no algorithm field in the token).
Exactly one algorithm can ever be used, and the token format carries no algorithm field for a caller to influence, so the "none" attack has no surface.
The verification key comes from the SESSION_SECRET environment variable alone; nothing in the token can point at another key source.
Expiry is checked on every decode, and an expired token is rejected rather than merely reported.

controls.rationale: The application encrypts nothing: it uses hashing and a MAC only, so there is no block mode or padding scheme in play.
No cipher is used anywhere; the only cryptography is password hashing and session signing.

controls.note: Only SHA-256 and scrypt with a per-user random salt and timingSafeEqual comparison are used; no MD5 or SHA-1 appears anywhere in the application.
The application speaks plain HTTP and configures no TLS versions of its own.
TLS is expected to terminate at a proxy this reference app does not ship.
No certificate is issued or configured by the application.
The build context excludes .git, so no source-control metadata reaches the deployable image.
Credentials travel in the request body and the session in a header or cookie; no URL or query string carries a secret.
Nothing clears the server-rendered DOM when the session ends, and no Clear-Site-Data header is sent.
No document states how quickly a vulnerable third-party component must be replaced.
The production dependency tree is audited in CI and ships with no unaddressed findings.
The login response returns a chosen subset of user fields; the password hash never leaves the data layer.
